feed.title: SHRINCS: 324-byte stateful post-quantum signatures with static backups

entry.title: SHRINCS: 324-byte stateful post-quantum signatures with static backups
entry.summary:
Recent benchmarking efforts have provided valuable insights into the performance of post-quantum signature schemes on SeedSigner’s off-the-shelf hardware boards. These experiments, conducted using methods and code detailed in the [report](https://kdmukai-bot.github.io/post-quantum-signature-benchmarks/), compared several cryptographic algorithms, including those referenced in Blockstream’s hardware wallet analysis, along with ML-DSA and FN-DSA. Five different boards from SeedSigner’s current and upcoming hardware lineup were evaluated to determine their suitability for implementing advanced post-quantum cryptography.
The benchmark results focused on signature schemes utilizing parameters aligned with the stateless path defined in the current [shrincs-bip](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip) draft. Specifically, the “SPHINCS+ 2^40” configuration employed SLH-DSA parameters (h=45, d=5, h'=9, k=10, a=13, w=16), resulting in 5,776-byte signatures. Timing these implementations on devices such as the Pi Zero 2 W, Pi Zero, ESP32-P4, ESP32-S3, and RP2350 revealed that signing operations could be completed in under eight seconds, even on the slowest board, with key generation times being notably faster.
A significant finding is that signing with the stateless SHRINCS implementation requires 21 to 22 percent less time compared to SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s across all tested boards, which closely matches the draft specification’s reduction in SHA-256 compressions by approximately 23 percent. This efficiency means that hardware wallets restored from a static seed backup are capable of executing stateless signatures within seconds, making them practical for real-world use even on resource-constrained devices.
It is important to note that the rows labeled SHRINCS-B and SHRINCS-L in the report correspond to earlier versions of Blockstream’s Jade code, which utilize different stateful parameters and a distinct PORS+FP stateless path. These measurements do not reflect the specifics of the current shrincs-bip draft and should not be conflated with its performance characteristics.
Overall, the results demonstrate that SeedSigner’s hardware is well-positioned to support modern post-quantum signature schemes, offering strong performance and responsiveness suitable for secure, user-friendly hardware wallet applications.
